text:
Ethan: ok this is a new one. moved apartments this weekend and apparently packed my router inside a suitcase. discovered at 8:45am when wifi died mid-standup. :sweat_smile: pic: /files/suitcase_router.jpg
Priya: oh nooo. why is your router on vacation with your socks? :joy:
Ethan: long story short: bathroom remodeling meant shelves off the wall and i shoved 'em all into a duffel. router, cables, little PoE switch included.
Marta: immediate triage: can you tether with your phone or borrow a travel router? I have a spare TP-Link mini that I can drop off if you're nearby.
Ethan: tethered and on audio-only for the first hour. standup survived. Jon offered a spare router earlier but i thought i was being clever. :facepalm:
Jon: still nearby. can swing by with the mini. also pro tip: label your cables. i have a drawer labeled "network" and the router never goes in luggage.
Timo: fun follow-up: if you packed the ISPs ONT/box too, please don't power it on in the new apartment until the ISP rep says so. weird configs can cause collisions.
Ethan: only the consumer router + switch + cables. left the ISP ONT installed. quick question: after i plug everything back, what commands should i run to verify?
Priya: `ip a` to check interfaces, `ping -c 4 8.8.8.8` for raw connectivity, and `dig +short txt debug.opendns.com \n` for DNS sanity. also `ethtool eth0` if you suspect speed/duplex flakiness.
Marta: and check LEDs on the router, they tell stories. if WAN light amber, modem handshake problem. if LAN link lights blink but no internet, try power-cycling modem first.
Ethan: plugging back in now.
status-bot: ticket created: HOME-2240 - "Router misplaced during move". add receipts if you buy a replacement.
Ethan: ok plugged in, WAN light solid, laptops got DHCP, `ping -c 4 8.8.8.8` shows 0% packet loss. crisis averted. thanks all.
Jon: yay. also i left the spare at your porch with a sticky note. label those boxes next time. :package:
Timo: reminder: if you file an expense for packing organizers or a small travel case specifically for networking gear, tag it Home Office Equipment.
Marta: also unsolicited: buy a small zip bag for all tiny adapters and a bright sticker so the router is not mistaken for a book next time.
Ethan: lesson learned. will never let the router vacation again. sending everyone a celebratory gif in DMs. :tada:
